text.title: Build-Generator Discipline — Decision Tree
text.summary: First gate: is there a generator between the sources and the shipped artefact? If so, each branch below names the one rule that closes the gap the observable reveals.

decision-tree.root-question: Does a build step turn source files into the artefact that ships, using templates, an external converter, or derived indexes?

branch.when: generator_exists == false OR (single_output == true AND external_converter == false AND derived_artefacts == 0)

conclusion.verdict: Skip. With no generator there is no drift to repair, no partial write to survive and no flavour to pin. Revisit the moment a second output or a derived index appears.
Fix this first — it is the only failure on the list that leaves the tree in a state no later run can diagnose. Render into a dict, write after the last render succeeds.
Add `--check` as its own entry point that renders into memory and compares against untouched disk. A check running after the build's own repair passes unconditionally.

Split it. Gate CI on the toolchain-free half (stamps, derived lists, manifests); keep the full re-render as a local pre-push gate. A CI gate that fails for reasons unrelated to the change gets disabled.
Restore autoescaping and reduce to one named exception. Route raw fragments through the same conversion path rather than widening the escape policy.
Make both fatal. An emptied source otherwise produces a structurally valid page with a header, a pager and nothing in it.
Pin the flavour and subtract unwanted extensions by name. A currency figure opening a TeX formula and eating the rest of the sentence is the canonical instance.
Add an explicit unpublished list and fail the build, naming any other unmapped source. Deliberate and forgotten must not look identical.
Read every number from the built artefact in the run that emits it. A transcribed measurement is correct once and re-checked never.
Verify the file and the assertion exist. If not, move the assertion into the generator's post-write verification rather than deleting the comment.
Run the build twice and confirm the second run prints zero repairs and produces no diff. Idempotence is what makes every other guarantee checkable.

example.trace: pandoc-backed static site, writes per page, no --check -> r2-render-all-before-writing-any first, then r6
